# Rich Opencode

Discord Rich Presence plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai). It shows what you are doing in OpenCode on your Discord profile. You choose what goes on each line.

```
Playing opencode
deepseek-v4.1-flash
↓ 298.8k | ↑ 398 · Working
01:23:45 elapsed
```

## What it does

The plugin reads OpenCode's event stream and session data. You place fields on either line, in any order, joined by the separator you pick.

Available fields:

| Field | Example | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | model ID |
| `modelName` | `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash` | display name from the model catalog |
| `provider` | `einfra` | provider ID |
| `variant` | `high` | model variant |
| `tokens` | `↓ 298.8k \| ↑ 398` | context usage or session totals |
| `tokenPercent` | `34%` | context used against the model limit |
| `cost` | `$0.52` | cumulative session cost |
| `status` | `Working` | Thinking, Working, Prompting or Idle |
| `project` | `Programming` | project folder name |
| `agent` | `build` | active agent ID |
| `title` | `Discord Rich Presence` | session title, visible on your profile |
| `text:<anything>` | `in opencode` | literal text |

## Requirements

- OpenCode 2.x. OpenCode 1.18.29 and newer also work.
- Discord desktop app running on the same machine. Discord in a browser cannot reach the local IPC socket.
- In Discord, open User Settings, then Activity Privacy, and turn on "Display current activity as a status message".
- Prompting requires macOS.

## Install with an AI agent

Point your agent at [AGENT_INSTALL.md](AGENT_INSTALL.md). It contains the commands, the config merge, verification and troubleshooting.

## Install manually

```bash
git clone https://github.com/YonCZ/OpenCode-Presence.git
cd rich-opencode
npm install
npm run build
```

Register the plugin in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. Use the absolute path to the checkout:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "/absolute/path/to/rich-opencode",
      "options": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

Save the file. OpenCode reloads the config. Then restart the background service and your TUI:

```bash
opencode service restart
```

Quit and reopen `opencode` after the restart. The service advertises the plugin's TUI part only after a fresh start, and the TUI loads it at startup. Your sessions stay intact.

The `options` object is optional. Every setting has a default.

## Configuration

All settings go in the `options` object of the plugin entry.

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "/absolute/path/to/rich-opencode",
      "options": {
        "details": ["model"],
        "state": ["tokens", "status"],
        "separator": " · ",
        "tokens": { "mode": "context" },
        "timer": { "enabled": true, "idleResetMinutes": 30 },
        "debug": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

`details` is the first line, `state` is the second line. Fields render in order, and empty fields are skipped.

### Options

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clientId` | built-in shared app | Discord Application ID |
| `details` | `["model"]` | fields on the first line |
| `state` | `["tokens", "status"]` | fields on the second line |
| `separator` | `" · "` | joins non-empty fields |
| `tokens.mode` | `"context"` | `context` matches OpenCode's sidebar, `cumulative` sums the session |
| `tokens.showInput` | `true` | show the input half |
| `tokens.showOutput` | `true` | show the output half |
| `tokens.inputPrefix` | `"↓"` | prefix for input tokens |
| `tokens.outputPrefix` | `"↑"` | prefix for output tokens |
| `cost.format` | `"${amount}"` | amount format, for example `"{amount} USD"` |
| `status.labels` | English labels | rename or translate the four states |
| `prompting.idleSeconds` | `60` | input within this window counts as prompting |
| `prompting.frontmostOnly` | `true` | require one of the apps below to be frontmost, macOS only |
| `prompting.apps` | Terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, Warp, VS Code, Cursor and others | apps that count as the opencode window |
| `timer.enabled` | `true` | show the elapsed timer |
| `timer.idleResetMinutes` | `30` | a continuous idle stretch this long starts a new timer |
| `largeImage.key` | `"logo"` | asset key for the large image |
| `largeImage.text` | `"OpenCode"` | hover text for the large image |
| `smallImage.enabled` | `false` | show a provider icon |
| `smallImage.providerIcons` | `{}` | icon URLs by provider ID |
| `debug` | `false` | write a log to `~/.local/share/opencode/rich-opencode-debug.log` |
| `leaderLock` | `true` | let one plugin instance use the Discord connection |

### Examples

Show the price:

```jsonc
"options": {
  "details": ["modelName"],
  "state": ["tokens", "cost", "status"],
  "cost": { "format": "${amount}" }
}
```

Custom status labels and separator:

```jsonc
"options": {
  "separator": " | ",
  "status": {
    "labels": {
      "thinking": "Thinking hard",
      "working": "Doing the thing",
      "prompting": "Your move",
      "idle": "Away"
    }
  }
}
```

## How it works

The plugin subscribes to the OpenCode V2 event stream.

| State | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Thinking | `session.reasoning.started` until `session.reasoning.ended` |
| Working | `session.execution.started`, tool calls, text streaming, step starts |
| Prompting | no agent activity, recent keyboard or mouse input, and the terminal is frontmost |
| Idle | nothing running and no recent input |

Token numbers come from `session.step.ended`, so the card shows the latest model call. The value matches the Context number in OpenCode's sidebar. The `cumulative` token mode uses the session totals instead.

The timer starts with the first activity and keeps counting through idle. A continuous idle stretch of `timer.idleResetMinutes` starts a new session timer, so opening an old chat does not show a 100 hour timer.

### Which chat is shown

The OpenCode server does not report focus changes. The plugin's TUI part writes the open chat to `~/.local/share/opencode/rich-opencode-focus.json` on route changes. The server reads that file.

- switching chats or tabs updates the card immediately
- a background chat that runs or finishes does not take over the card
- switching between terminal windows without changing the chat cannot be detected. Open the chat or send a prompt and the card updates.
- if the TUI part is missing, the plugin falls back to the session that ran last

### Prompting

OpenCode does not send prompt typing to plugins. The TUI keeps the draft local, and `tui.prompt.append` is an inbound command. Prompting therefore uses macOS system idle time and the frontmost app. It appears only when you used the keyboard or mouse in the last 60 seconds and the terminal is frontmost. On other platforms this state stays off.

### Multiple instances

OpenCode loads one plugin instance per project location. The `leaderLock` option lets one instance use the Discord connection, with a lock file at `~/.local/share/opencode/rich-opencode.lock`. The leader retries the Discord handshake with backoff if it times out.

## Custom Discord app

1. Create an application at [discord.com/developers/applications](https://discord.com/developers/applications). The app name becomes the "Playing" headline.
2. Copy the Application ID and set it as `clientId`.
3. Open Rich Presence, then Art Assets, and upload your large image with the key used by `largeImage.key`. The default key is `logo`.
4. Optional: upload provider icons and map them in `smallImage.providerIcons`.

## Development

```bash
npm run build       # compile to dist/
npm run typecheck   # type check only
npm run preview     # show a sample card in Discord for 5 seconds
npm run diagnose    # open one raw RPC connection for 10 minutes
```

Set `"debug": true` to write a log to `~/.local/share/opencode/rich-opencode-debug.log`. The log rotates at 5 MB.

# Agent installation

Instructions for an AI coding agent. The user asked you to install Rich Opencode, a Discord Rich Presence plugin for OpenCode. Follow the steps in order. Stop and report the failing step instead of guessing.

## Rules

- Back up the OpenCode config before you edit it.
- Keep the user's existing config keys and plugin entries.
- Do not ask for a Discord password or token. The plugin talks to the local Discord app.
- Do not restart the OpenCode TUI yourself. Ask the user to restart it at the end.

## 1. Check the environment

Run these commands:

```bash
opencode --version
node --version
```

Required:

- OpenCode 2.x, or OpenCode 1.18.29 and newer
- Node 20 or newer

Check that the Discord desktop app is installed and running. On macOS:

```bash
ls /Applications/Discord.app
pgrep -f "Discord.app/Contents/MacOS/Discord" >/dev/null && echo running
```

If Discord is not running, start it and wait a few seconds. Discord in a browser will not work.

## 2. Clone and build

Install into a stable directory:

```bash
DIR="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/rich-opencode"

# update if already installed
if [ -d "$DIR/.git" ]; then
  git -C "$DIR" pull --ff-only
else
  git clone https://github.com/YonCZ/OpenCode-Presence.git "$DIR"
fi

cd "$DIR"
npm install
npm run build
test -f "$DIR/dist/index.js" && echo "build ok"
```

If the build fails, stop and report the compiler output.

## 3. Register the plugin

The plugin is loaded from a local path, so add it to the global OpenCode config at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.

Back up the file first:

```bash
cp ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json.bak 2>/dev/null || true
```

Merge the plugin entry with this script. It keeps existing keys and entries, and removes an older entry for the same path. The script strips JSONC comments when it rewrites the file.

```bash
DIR="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/rich-opencode" python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os

path = os.path.expanduser("~/.config/opencode/opencode.json")
target = os.path.abspath(os.environ["DIR"])

def strip_comments(text):
    out, i, in_string, escape = [], 0, False, False
    while i < len(text):
        ch = text[i]
        if in_string:
            out.append(ch)
            if escape:
                escape = False
            elif ch == "\\":
                escape = True
            elif ch == '"':
                in_string = False
            i += 1
            continue
        if ch == '"':
            in_string = True
            out.append(ch)
            i += 1
            continue
        if ch == "/" and i + 1 < len(text) and text[i + 1] == "/":
            while i < len(text) and text[i] != "\n":
                i += 1
            continue
        if ch == "/" and i + 1 < len(text) and text[i + 1] == "*":
            i += 2
            while i + 1 < len(text) and not (text[i] == "*" and text[i + 1] == "/"):
                i += 1
            i += 2
            continue
        out.append(ch)
        i += 1
    return "".join(out)

if os.path.exists(path):
    with open(path) as f:
        data = json.loads(strip_comments(f.read()))
else:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    data = {"$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"}

plugins = data.get("plugins")
if not isinstance(plugins, list):
    plugins = []

def is_target(entry):
    spec = entry if isinstance(entry, str) else entry.get("package") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
    return isinstance(spec, str) and os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(spec)) == target

plugins = [entry for entry in plugins if not is_target(entry)]
plugins.append({"package": target, "options": {}})
data["plugins"] = plugins

with open(path, "w") as f:
    json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
    f.write("\n")

print("registered", target)
PY
```

The resulting entry:

```json
{
  "package": "/Users/you/.local/share/rich-opencode",
  "options": {}
}
```

## 4. Verify the plugin loads

```bash
opencode api get /api/plugin 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"id":"rich-opencode"'
```

If nothing prints, restart the background service and try again:

```bash
opencode service restart
sleep 5
opencode api get /api/plugin 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"id":"rich-opencode"'
```

Expected output is `"id":"rich-opencode"`. The plugin state should be `active`.

## 5. Ask the user for the Discord setting

You cannot enable this setting for the user. Tell them:

1. Open Discord.
2. Open User Settings with the gear icon.
3. Open Activity Privacy.
4. Turn on "Display current activity as a status message".

## 6. Restart the service and the TUI

The service caches the plugin feature list from the first load. A fresh start advertises the TUI part. Run:

```bash
opencode service restart
sleep 5
opencode api get /api/plugin 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"id":"rich-opencode","source":{[^}]*},"features":{[^}]*}'
```

The features should include `"tui":true`.

Then tell the user to quit and reopen `opencode`. The plugin includes a TUI part that reports the open chat, and the TUI loads it at startup. Their sessions and the background service stay intact.

## Troubleshooting

No presence on the profile:

- Confirm Discord desktop is running.
- Confirm the Activity Privacy setting above is on.
- Run `cd "$DIR" && npm run diagnose`. This opens one raw connection and shows a diagnostic card for 10 minutes.
- Ask the user to view their profile from a second account. Discord sometimes hides your own activity from you.

Wrong chat or stale model:

- The TUI was not restarted after install. The focus file `~/.local/share/opencode/rich-opencode-focus.json` is written by the TUI part.

Plugin not listed:

- Check `opencode --version`. Version 1 requires 1.18.29 or newer.
- Run `cd "$DIR" && npm run typecheck` and report errors.
- Set `"debug": true` in the plugin options, then read `~/.local/share/opencode/rich-opencode-debug.log` after a few minutes.

## Update

```bash
DIR="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/rich-opencode"
git -C "$DIR" pull --ff-only
cd "$DIR" && npm install && npm run build
```

## Uninstall

Remove the entry from `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` and delete the directory:

```bash
DIR="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/rich-opencode"
python3 - "$DIR" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys
path = os.path.expanduser("~/.config/opencode/opencode.json")
target = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1])
data = json.load(open(path))
plugins = data.get("plugins") or []
def is_target(entry):
    spec = entry if isinstance(entry, str) else entry.get("package") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
    return isinstance(spec, str) and os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(spec)) == target
data["plugins"] = [entry for entry in plugins if not is_target(entry)]
json.dump(data, open(path, "w"), indent=2)
PY
rm -rf "$DIR"
```

Then restart the service with `opencode service restart` and the TUI.
